comment: Clean has no `override` keyword; it has typeclasses. `class Show a where show ::` declares `show` ABSTRACT and `instance Show Thing where show t = ...` supplies it, so at type `Thing` the compiler selects the instance's `show` in place of the class's. That is the relation the F# lane reads off the `override` keyword (real-fsharp-analyzer.ts:656-669) and the Haskell lane's doc records as `overrides T.m -> C.m` (haskell.md:57). Clean has no keyword to probe, so the pairing is derived from two `name` fields. Measured before the branch existed: 1,036 instance members across 78 classes at the 2,181-file corpus (`script/m14/clean-extends-overrides-probe.ts`, instrument B1), so the type was a GAP and not an absence. The guard is IN-FILE — `Forbidden` below is the negative half: an instance for an IMPORTED class emits no `overrides`, because the edge claims this member implements THAT CLASS MEMBER and an un-read declaration is not a claim the analyzer may make.

expectSymbols.name: Show
expectSymbols.comment: a class_declaration publishes as an Interface

expectSymbols.name: show
expectSymbols.comment: the class member — ABSTRACT, no body

expectSymbols.name: Thing::instance
expectSymbols.comment: the instance container, NAMESPACED under its target (`<target>::instance`, the Rust lane's `<target>::impl`). It used to be named exactly `Thing`, which made this file a second DECLARATION of `Thing` — a phantom, and the reason 366 `references` rows on the 312-file population were ambiguous. The members below keep the NOMINAL owner, so every edge endpoint is unchanged.

expectSymbols.name: show
expectSymbols.comment: the instance member that supplies Show.show

expectSymbols.name: Int::instance
expectSymbols.comment: `instance Show Int` — the container is `Int::instance`, and its member is still owned by `Int`

expectSymbols.name: size
expectSymbols.comment: `size` is NOT a Show member, so this instance member overrides nothing

expectRelationships.comment: instance-member -> class-member, QUALIFIED on both sides, on the member's OWN name line (M59.O2)
two instances of one class: two edges at two lines. A per-set dedupe keyed on source|type|target would keep one and fail the other
the instance-level edge, unchanged: `overrides` is the MEMBER refinement of it, not a replacement

forbidRelationships.comment: `size` is not in Show's member set, so this instance member overrides NOTHING — the edge would name a class member that does not exist
the mirror of the above: no edge may point at a class member the class does not declare
the direction is instance-member -> class-member, never the reverse: the class member is abstract and overrides nothing
endpoints are QUALIFIED. A bare `show` collides with the module-level `show` in every consumer, so an unqualified edge is a different defect and is forbidden too

SELF-EDGE REFUSAL. `instance Sized a` publishes no symbol of its own (its target is the type VARIABLE `a`), so its members are attributed to the CLASS and `instanceType === className`. The composed endpoints would be identical and the edge would read `Sized.size -> Sized.size` — a declaration overriding itself. Measured on the corpus before this guard: 60 such self-edges, every one from a polymorphic instance of a locally-declared class (`instance List [] a where _cons …` in clean-stdlib/_SystemStrictLists.icl).
the mirror of the above: the class member `Sized.size` is abstract and overrides nothing in either direction
